subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a capillary, substances such as glucose and oxygen leave the blood by which process?
options: Diffusion across the thin capillary wall
questions.explain: Substances diffuse between blood and tissues across the one-cell-thick capillary walls.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly shows blood flow through the right side of the heart?
options: Vena cava then right atrium then right ventricle then pulmonary artery
Aorta then left atrium then right ventricle then lungs
Pulmonary vein then right ventricle then aorta
Right atrium then left ventricle then vena cava
questions.explain: Deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium, passes to the right ventricle and out via the pulmonary artery.

questions.q: Which large vein returns deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart?
questions.explain: The vena cava carries deoxygenated blood from the body back into the right atrium.

questions.q: Which part of the blood mainly transports dissolved substances such as carbon dioxide, urea and nutrients?
questions.explain: Plasma is the liquid that transports dissolved substances around the body.

questions.q: From which chamber does oxygenated blood leave the heart into the aorta?
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta to the body.

questions.q: What is the function of valves in the heart and veins?
questions.explain: Valves ensure blood flows in one direction only and prevent backflow.

questions.q: Through which blood vessels does the heart muscle itself receive oxygen?
questions.explain: The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle with oxygenated blood.

questions.q: Why is the human circulatory system described as 'double'?
options: Blood passes through the heart twice for each full circuit of the body
It carries blood in two colours
questions.explain: Blood travels through the heart twice per circuit: once to the lungs and once to the body.

questions.q: Which feature is typical of arteries?
options: Thick muscular elastic walls to withstand high pressure
They carry blood towards the heart
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, so they have thick, elastic walls.

questions.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
options: It pumps blood at high pressure all around the body
It pumps blood only to the lungs
questions.explain: The left ventricle must generate enough pressure to pump blood around the whole body.

questions.q: What does haemoglobin combine with to transport oxygen?
questions.explain: Haemoglobin binds oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin in the lungs and releases it in the tissues.

questions.q: Which blood component carries oxygen?
questions.explain: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds and transports oxygen.

questions.q: What is the role of white blood cells?
questions.explain: White blood cells are part of the immune system, destroying pathogens by phagocytosis and antibodies.

questions.q: Which side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood?
questions.explain: The right side of the heart receives and pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

questions.q: Why is it an advantage that mammals have a double circulatory system?
options: The heart only beats once per minute
Blood pressure can be kept high to the body after passing through the lungs
questions.explain: Returning blood to the heart after the lungs lets it be repumped at high pressure to the body.

questions.q: Why do capillaries have walls that are one cell thick?
options: To allow efficient exchange of substances by short diffusion distance
questions.explain: Thin capillary walls give a short diffusion path for exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste.

questions.q: Which vessel returns oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explain: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the heart.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explain: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

questions.q: What is the main role of platelets?
questions.explain: Platelets are cell fragments that help the blood clot at wounds.

questions.q: Compared with arteries, veins generally have...
options: Thinner walls, a wider lumen and valves
Thick muscular walls and no lumen
Thicker walls and a narrower lumen
questions.explain: Veins carry blood at low pressure, so they have thinner walls, a wide lumen and valves.

questions.q: How are red blood cells adapted to carry oxygen?
options: They can change shape to engulf bacteria
They have a nucleus packed with DNA
They are biconcave and have no nucleus, giving more room for haemoglobin
questions.explain: Red blood cells lack a nucleus and are biconcave, maximising space and surface area for haemoglobin.

questions.q: Which chambers of the heart receive blood returning to the heart?
questions.explain: The atria are the upper chambers that receive blood entering the heart.
